title: Urinary catheter care

sources.use: Recommendation sections I-III read in full text in Phase 7 (2009; PDF footer last update June 2019); other sections not read

objectives: Describe appropriate indications and the aim of minimising catheter days.
Maintain a closed drainage system and unobstructed flow.

items.text: Insert catheters only for appropriate indications and leave them only as long as needed (Category IB). Examples include acute retention or outlet obstruction, accurate urine-output measurement in critically ill patients, and prolonged immobilisation; the indications are expert consensus.
Avoid catheters for managing incontinence (IB); consider external catheters in cooperative men without retention (Category II).
Hand hygiene immediately before and after insertion or any manipulation of the catheter or site (IB).
Only trained persons who know aseptic insertion and maintenance do this (IB); in acute care use aseptic technique and sterile equipment (IB).
Maintain a closed drainage system; if aseptic technique breaks, or the system disconnects or leaks, replace the catheter and collecting system aseptically (IB).
Use Standard Precautions, including gloves and gown as appropriate, during any manipulation (IB).

Secure the catheter to prevent movement and urethral traction (IB); keep the catheter and tubing free from kinking, the bag below bladder level at all times and off the floor (IB); empty the bag regularly with a separate clean container per patient, avoiding splashing and spigot contact (IB).
Who inserts, changes and removes catheters, and nurse-led removal protocols, follow local policy.

Assess and document the ongoing need for the catheter daily, as part of the unit's review process, and remove it as soon as it is no longer indicated (Category IB) rather than leaving it until a routine fixed interval.

Sterile gloves, drape, sponges, an appropriate antiseptic or sterile solution for periurethral cleaning and a single-use lubricant packet for insertion; use the smallest bore catheter consistent with good drainage unless otherwise indicated (IB; II).
The step-by-step insertion sequence is not in the recommendation sections read; follow the competency-approved unit procedure.

Do not change catheters or bags at routine fixed intervals; change for infection, obstruction or a compromised closed system (Category II). Do not clean the periurethral area with antiseptics while the catheter is in place; routine hygiene is appropriate (IB).
When a small fresh urine sample is clinically indicated, obtain it aseptically from the disinfected needleless sampling port under the local procedure; do not use the drainage bag for urine culture.

Report fever, new pain, haematuria, obstruction or a compromised drainage system and assess the patient for other causes of deterioration. Cloudiness or odour alone does not establish infection or justify routine cultures or antibiotics; follow the local culture-stewardship and clinical-assessment pathway.
Catheter-associated urinary tract infection, urethral trauma and obstruction.
Record indication, insertion details, daily review of need and removal date per unit standard.

checklist.text: Confirm an appropriate indication exists and ask each day whether the catheter is still needed.
Perform hand hygiene before and after any manipulation.
Keep the system closed; replace the catheter and system aseptically after a break, disconnection or leak.
Keep tubing free from kinks and the bag below bladder level and off the floor.
Secure the catheter to prevent traction.
Empty the bag with a separate clean container per patient without touching the spigot.

Report obstruction, new pain, fever, haematuria or systemic deterioration. Cloudy or malodorous urine alone is not a diagnosis; seek clinical assessment rather than automatically requesting a culture.
Record indication, daily review and removal date.
For a clinically indicated urine culture, use the disinfected sampling port and aseptic local procedure, not the drainage bag.
